decisions.decision: The blank batch-log page carries the whole battery, split into 'At the machine' and 'When you taste it', printed two pages front and back of one sheet
decisions.rationale: Mark: the current printout is already 4+ sheets, so a duplex churn log is acceptable. The split matches the app's own seam - BatchRow.jsx already groups the battery into a churn section and a tasting section.

decisions.decision: The sheet's short code is derived from the version id, not a per-print random nonce
decisions.rationale: Mark: the goal is to track the print back to the recipe version. The batch record is created when recorded, not when printed - settled in his background research. A derived code stores nothing and leaves D16 untouched. Accepted loss: two printings of one unchanged version are indistinguishable.

decisions.decision: Printing lives on its own route, /recipe/:id/sheet, not print CSS on the recipe page
decisions.rationale: Mark: printing will have multiple modes (recipe development vs publishing/sharing); a separate route fits that, and burdening the already-complex recipe route would make it worse. router.jsx already anticipated a Phase 4 print route. Milestone 1 builds the bench sheet mode only - no mode switcher.

decisions.decision: A split row prints one line per portion in each step's group, each with its own mise-en-place tick and as-made blank
decisions.rationale: Asserted rather than asked, then confirmed: the maker weighs each portion separately at the bench, and the sheet's '120 g + 263 g' is already what paper does. Follows the 2026-09-09 portions revision that retired the Step column.

decisions.decision: Keep both Save ceremony mounts with identical labels; the brief is the stale document, not the code
decisions.rationale: Mark: two identical Saves are intentional redundancy on a long page; the brief's two-scope idea ('Save batch only' / 'Save batch & tasting') is what was wrong. Requires a brief revision, not a code change.

decisions.decision: Address all five critique issues in impact order 1 -> 3 -> 4 -> 2 -> 5
decisions.rationale: Mark chose the full scope over either sub-group. Issues 1, 2 and 5 are all /impeccable harden on one component and would sensibly batch into one /gsd-quick-batch.
